verdict.rationale: Apple documents a 16-core CPU for M4 Max and claims up to 2.1x faster Xcode build performance than M1 Max. A community Geekbench multi-core comparison shows it beating a 13900K, which corroborates strong parallel throughput. Verification doubts about Geekbench submissions are general skepticism, not a concrete counter-example. missing for 10: documented boost/clock behavior, independent rigorous multi-core or large-codebase compile benchmarks beyond a single user-posted Geekbench link.

support.subject: As a developer, I can compile big codebases and run heavy parallel jobs fast — documented core counts and boost behavior, corroborated by independent multi-core benchmarks

citations.quote: M4 Max with 16-core CPU and 40-core GPU (546GB/s memory bandwidth)
Up to 2.1x faster build performance when compiling code in Xcode when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max
Wild. It absolutely shits on my 13900K - https://browser.geekbench.com/v6/cpu/compare/7692643?baseline=8593555
